_comment: Package hall (QA Nov 14): the great hall's seating, the bandstand and the live broadcast position. Same shape as props.json; generate.py adds STYLE to every prompt. Run with RODIN_PROPS_FILE=tools/rodin/props_hall.json. Cap: 9 generations.
style: 1940s American period piece, realistic proportions, single object seen whole, centred, matte, neutral flat lighting, no baked shadows, no text, no logos, plain background

props.hall_chair: a 1940s hotel ballroom side chair of the kind set out in rows for an auction, a gilded wooden frame with four slim straight legs, a padded burgundy velvet seat and a padded upholstered upright rectangular back framed in gilt, plain and solid
props.hall_tvcamera: a large late 1940s black and white television studio camera like the RCA TK-30: a boxy dark grey metal camera body with a rotating turret of four round lenses on its front, a hooded viewfinder on top, two side handles at the back, mounted on a heavy tall studio pedestal column with a three-wheeled castor base
props.hall_drums: a 1940s swing big band drum kit: a large bass drum with a plain cream front head, a snare drum on a stand, a small mounted tom, a floor tom on legs, a hi-hat stand and one large ride cymbal on a stand, black lacquer shells with chrome hardware
props.hall_bass: an upright double bass standing upright on its endpin, dark varnished brown maple body with a spruce top and two f-holes, a long black fingerboard up the neck, a carved scroll and tuning pegs at the top, four strings over a wooden bridge
props.hall_mic: a 1940s broadcast ribbon microphone with a large oblong chrome grille like the RCA 44, on a tall slim chrome floor stand with a heavy round cast-iron base
props.hall_phone: a 1940s black bakelite desk telephone with a rotary dial on the front and the handset resting in a cradle on top
props.hall_monitor: a late 1940s television studio monitor: a dark metal cabinet with a small rounded black and white picture tube screen on its front, standing on a tall four-legged metal stand
props.hall_micstand: a 1940s big band singer microphone stand: a small chrome broadcast microphone with an oblong slotted grille mounted at the very top of a long thin straight chrome pole, the stand about ten times taller than the microphone, a heavy round cast-iron base on the floor
